turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I came in because... I just feel like I’m crawling out of my skin, you know? Whenever I’m supposed to sit still, like in the radiology suite at work, or even in my college classes. Which, by the way, the seats in my anatomy lecture hall are the absolute worst. They're these tiny plastic things attached to the desks, and I swear they were designed for people half my size. The guy who sits next to me always brings this huge iced coffee and leaves the condensation ring right where I need to put my arm. Anyway, yeah, I've been trying to tough it out for months, just telling myself to sit down and focus, but I still end up pacing around the room, or shifting in my seat constantly, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move. Like, I'll volunteer to go restock the lead aprons just to walk down the hall. Lead aprons are super heavy, by the way, but I'd rather lug those around than sit in that chair for another minute.

turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, it’s definitely not a new thing. My parents actually still bring up my old elementary school parent-teacher conferences. They used to hold those in the cafeteria, and my mom always complained about the tiny chairs they had to sit in—which is funny because now I'm the one complaining about tiny chairs in my college lectures! I don't know why schools can't just buy normal-sized furniture. 

But anyway, yeah, at those conferences the teachers were always saying how I was constantly out of my seat. And I was always calling out, or I'd be rushing ahead on the worksheets before they even finished giving the directions. I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Higgins, she had this really weird rule where we had to use red pens for math. I still don't know why, it just made all our worksheets look like they were bleeding. But yeah, I’d just speed through the math problems in red ink before she even stopped talking about how to do them. 

So all of that was happening way before middle school. It's definitely not just something that popped up since I started my radiology training.

turns.patient_response: Careless mistakes? I mean... I don't really think so? Like, I don't feel like I'm missing things or messing up details. Honestly, my biggest issue is just the sitting.
